questions.title: Pyramidal cells with basophilic base and acidophilic apex
questions.question: Which structure consists of pyramidal cells with ill defined boundaries where the apical part is acidophilic and the basal part is basophilic?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Mucous acinar cells are pale-staining with sharply defined cell boundaries — the opposite polarity and appearance from the cells described.
explanations.B: Correct. Serous acinar cells are pyramidal with poorly defined lateral boundaries. Basal cytoplasm is basophilic, reflecting the abundant rough endoplasmic reticulum making the protein-rich secretion, while the apical cytoplasm is acidophilic, reflecting the zymogen (secretory) granules stored there before release.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Myoepithelial cells are flattened, contractile basket cells that surround acini and ducts to help expel secretion — a different cell type from the secretory acinar cell described.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Endocrine follicles (as in the thyroid) store colloid within a lumen and secrete internally into the bloodstream, a different structural arrangement from an exocrine serous acinus.

questions.learning_objective: Describe the serous acinus's pyramidal cells with basophilic base and acidophilic apex.
